description: Your company's portfolio risk calculator in production_code.py has a bug in IRR calculation when cash flows contain very small values near zero (e.g., 0.000001). The bug occurs in numpy_financial's irr() function. Your task: Create a minimal reproducible example (MRE) suitable for reporting to the numpy-financial maintainers. Create file /home/ga/workspace/portfolio_risk/bug_report_mre.py containing a self-contained Python script (max 25 lines of code, excluding comments) that: (1) imports only numpy and numpy_financial, (2) demonstrates the bug with a minimal example, (3) includes comments explaining expected vs actual behavior, (4) prints output showing the issue. Also create /home/ga/workspace/portfolio_risk/BUG_REPORT.md containing: a clear title, environment info (library versions), expected behavior section, actual behavior section, and reproduction steps. The MRE should isolate just the core bug - remove all business logic, database code, risk models, and internal dependencies from the production code. Focus on the _normalize_currency method which returns the problematic array: [-1000, 0.000001, 0.000001, 0.000001, 1000.5]. This pattern triggers the bug when passed to npf.irr().
